labels.label: bzdef:c2s2d1_mesure_projective

hypotheses.note: S(E) and GSE E for any real vector space E (S n is E = R^(n+1))

hypotheses.paper: A, A', B', B four points of a segment (AB), met in this order from A to B
hypotheses.note: projMeasure_eq_log assumes B ≠ A, B ≠ -A, A', B' in the open segment and B' ∈ (A', B); the definition itself is total (⊤ outside its domain, see questions)

IsCrossRatio is a relation (odds form); isCrossRatio_affine shows it is the classical ratio of algebraic measures (pr/qr)(qs/ps) on any affine line, the formula of p. 250 with the transcription's [sic] read

questions: Déf. 1 (l.262–268) leaves two kinds of degenerate configuration, and the measure is ⊤ in both. (i) A' = A with B' ≠ A, or B' = B with A' ≠ B: the printed formula (pr/qr)(qs/ps) has a zero denominator and a nonzero numerator, so the cross-ratio is infinite. Here ⊤ = log ∞ is the printed value extended, not a reading. (ii) Coincident points: A' = B' = A or A' = B' = B, where the formula is 0/0, or A = B, four equal points. Here the paper defines no cross-ratio, and ⊤ is a convention (projMeasure_left_eq_top, _right_eq_top, _same_eq_top). Case (ii) changes nothing for n ≥ 1, because a point M is interior to a segment of a chart, so IsMajoreSeg n k {M} M M ↔ 0 < k under either convention. It matters only in dimension 0; see the question under bzdef:c2s2d3_pseudo_longueur. Déf. 1's own printed claims (≥ 1, GS-invariance, measure = log of the cross-ratio) never reach these configurations, so Déf. 1's mark does not depend on either case.

Déf. 2 (l.277–282) applies the measure to φ(A', B') ⊂ φ(A, B) without saying which inner point plays A'. Reading taken: the measure is |log (A', B', B, A)|, which is log (A', B', B, A) ≥ 0 in the printed order (projMeasure_eq_log) and does not depend on the naming of the inner points (projMeasure_swap) nor on the direction of (A, B) (projMeasure_reverse).

labels.label: bzprop:c2s2p1_mesure_projective_monotone

hypotheses.paper: (A'', B'') contenu dans (A', B'); AB remplacé par un segment le contenant
hypotheses.note: projMeasure_le_inner only needs A'', B'' ∈ (A', B'), projMeasure_le_outer only A, B ∈ (A₁, B₁), with no order or position hypothesis on A', B'; projMeasure_antitone states the printed inclusions

findings: Prop. 1 (l.270–273) has no printed proof (l.274). It is true and proved here in a stronger form. The proof: the cross-ratio (A', B', B, A) is odds(B')/odds(A') in coordinates on (A, B), and every point of (A', B') has odds between those of A' and B'. Hence |log (v/u)| ≤ |log r| for u, v between 1 and r.

hypotheses.paper: (A', B') un segment d'une variété localement projective V
hypotheses.note: IsProjSegment n Sg' A' B' is the first conjunct; V is [ChartedSpace (S n) V], with [HasGroupoid V (projGroupoid n)] in the theorems

hypotheses.paper: « si φ est une carte compatible d'un voisinage de (A, B) sur un ouvert de S(n), on ait »
hypotheses.note: every compatible chart φ with Sg ⊆ φ.source is quantified, as printed; this is equivalent to the existential reading (isMajoreSeg_iff_exists_chart), by Ch. 1 Prop. 1's chart change on the connected segment and the GS-invariance of the measure, so no reading is needed

labels.label: bzdef:c2s2d3_pseudo_longueur

hypotheses.paper: « la borne inférieure des nombres k »
hypotheses.note: an infimum over real k in EReal (⊤ for an empty set); for n ≥ 1 the set is nonempty for every segment (pseudoLength_lt_top)

questions: Déf. 3 (l.284–287) defines l_V(M, N) for « un segment (M, N) ». In a manifold two points can be joined by several segments, so the notation is read as a function of the segment (the set together with its two endpoints), not of the pair of points: pseudoLength n Sg M N.

Dimension 0, a question with three choices for the author, not a finding as such. Property 1° of the enonce (l.232, « l_V(M, M) = 0 ») is not literally true for n = 0. The reason is that Déf. 1 assigns no measure to coincident points, and in dimension 0 that is the only configuration. S(0) has two diametrically opposite points (S0_eq_or_eq_neg), so every segment is a point, and its only majorising candidate is itself (A = B). Hence no k majorises (M, M), and l(M, M) = +∞ (pseudoLength_self_eq_top_dim_zero, stated on V = S(0); the same proof works on every V charted on S(0), a single point included). 1° holds for n ≥ 1 (pseudoLength_self), and it would hold in every dimension if a point were given measure 0. The paper never says n ≥ 1, and Ch. 1 even names S(0) (ch1 l.192). The three choices: (a) n ≥ 1 is implied; (b) a point has measure 0, so 1° holds for every n; (c) a finding as printed. The Lean follows the literal text, giving ⊤. Prop. 3 (T-bz-c2-hilbert) inherits the same question: with this convention a point of a 0-manifold has no majorised neighbourhood. The question concerns the row bzthm:c2s2_proprietes_pseudo_longueur (T-bz-c2-proprietes) and Prop. 3.

hypotheses.paper: deux points quelconques de C joints par un segment inclus dans C et majoré par k dans V

kb_proposals: The cross-ratio and projective measure of S(E) are in BenzecriScaffold.Chapter2.CrossRatio (Mathlib has none). IsCrossRatio A' B' B A r is the odds form: there are representatives a, b with a+b representing A' and a+r•b representing B'. Compute it with isCrossRatio_of_coords (r = odds(B')/odds(A')) or isCrossRatio_affine (the classical (pr/qr)(qs/ps)). projMeasure is EReal-valued and ⊤ on degenerate quadruples.

Points and segments of S(E) in coordinates: Sphere.IsRep v x (v ∈ F(x)). mem_closedSeg_iff and mem_openSeg_iff turn segment membership into nonnegative (resp. positive) combinations of representatives. B ≠ A ∧ B ≠ -A iff the representatives are independent (linearIndependent_of_ne, ne_of_linearIndependent).

Chart change on a segment of a locally projective manifold: exists_smul_eq_on_of_isPreconnected (two compatible charts differ by one g ∈ GS on a connected set in both sources) with IsProjSegment.isPreconnected_seg. IsProjSegment.image_eq_closedSeg says every compatible chart maps a segment onto the segment of its endpoints. T-bz-c2-poches proved the same lemmas through IsGXSegment, so dedupe at graduation.

Building majorised segments: isMajoreSeg_of_chart needs one chart φ with (a', b') ⊆ (a, b) ⊆ φ.target and measure < k. exists_closedSeg_extend extends a segment of S(n) lying in an open set beyond both endpoints, using the tube lemma on (ε, t).
Pitfall: `rintro _ rfl` on `x ∈ {M}` eliminates the variable M (not x) and breaks later references to M. Rewrite with mem_singleton_iff and `rw [hx]` instead.
notes: Two new modules, a chain: Mesure imports CrossRatio. I typechecked them with the kb/0034 recipe (/tmp oleans, since deleted). At the end I ran `lake build BenzecriScaffold.Chapter2.CrossRatio BenzecriScaffold.Chapter2.Mesure` after checking that no other build was running. Only these two modules were compiled; nothing upstream was rebuilt. There is no sorry, and #print axioms gives {propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound} for every principal declaration. The scaffold root BenzecriScaffold.lean was not edited, so the new modules are invisible to the axiom sweep until the root imports them (lean-causal kb/0025). Properties 1°–4° of the enonce bzthm:c2s2_proprietes_pseudo_longueur are proved as UNMARKED lemmas, for T-bz-c2-proprietes (OQ-38(a)). 1° is pseudoLength_nonneg (no hypothesis) and pseudoLength_self (n ≥ 1), with the counterexample pseudoLength_self_eq_top_dim_zero for n = 0. 2° is pseudoLength_smul, for g : GXAut (GSR n) (S n) V. 3° is pseudoLength_mono, which uses Prop. 1's first assertion. 4° is pseudoLength_le_opens for a segment of V' and pseudoLength_le_opens' for a segment of V included in V'; it is proved directly, not through Prop. 1. NAME COLLISION AVOIDED: the parallel T-bz-c2-poches file declares Sphere.isPreconnected_closedSeg, IsProjSegment.isPreconnected and IsProjSegment.image_eq. Mine had the same full names and are renamed isPreconnected_closedSeg_of_ne_neg, isPreconnected_seg and image_eq_closedSeg, so both modules can be imported together. The content is duplicated, as is gse_image_closedSeg / gse_smul_neg against Poches' Sphere.GSE.image_smul_closedSeg / Sphere.GSE.smul_neg. Keep one copy at graduation. MARKS: the five labels are marked, and AUDIT-1 (minor) confirms them. The only convention with consequences is the coincident-point case (Déf. 1, case (ii): ⊤ for A' = B' at an endpoint, or A = B). It acts through IsMajoreSeg. If the author rules it a reading, then Déf. 2, Déf. 3 and Déf. 4 become partial, in dimension 0 only. Déf. 1 and Prop. 1 are unaffected. The case A' = A with B' ≠ A (or B' = B with A' ≠ B) is the printed ∞ and binds no label. The orientation-free |log| is absorbed by the existential over the naming of (A, B) in Déf. 2. PASS ON: the n = 0 question (three choices: n ≥ 1 implied / a point has measure 0 / a finding as printed) must reach the T-bz-c2-proprietes dispatch (property 1°) and the T-bz-c2-hilbert dispatch (Prop. 3, which fails at n = 0 under the same convention). FIX ROUND 1 (after AUDIT-1, no statement or proof changed): the n = 0 finding is reworded as a question with three choices, in the Mesure docstring (checklist, SCOPE « Dimension 0 », the docstrings of pseudoLength_self and pseudoLength_self_eq_top_dim_zero) and here. The fallback above is corrected. CrossRatio's SCOPE and the docstrings of projMeasure, projMeasure_left_eq_top, projMeasure_right_eq_top and projMeasure_same_eq_top now separate the infinite case from the 0/0 case. Upstream candidates (general S(E) facts): IsRep and its API, mem_closedSeg_iff, mem_openSeg_iff, closedSeg_self, closedSeg_subset_closedSeg, linearIndependent_of_ne, isPreconnected_closedSeg_of_ne_neg, gse_image_closedSeg.
